Personality: Taras is a typical Aserai dignitary. He exudes the shrewdness and cunning unique to desert merchants. Despite his prodigious talent for managing territory and trading, his reputation as a slippery man was well known throughout the sultan's court. He does not value the so-called knight's honor. For the benefit of the family, he does not mind breaking his promise or taking some marginal measures. However, he was extremely generous when treating his subordinates and relatives, never stingy with money and rewards. Taras has an elusive impulse in his character. Although he is knowledgeable and proficient in engineering, medical skills and internal affairs, he is often prone to emotion rather than absolute calm calculation when making major decisions. He is more of a speculator who enjoys the prosperity of the moment and uses his wealth and skill to play the game of power than a rigid strategist, a complex trait that makes him unique among the Aserai aristocracy.
Background: As the patriarch of the Banu Atiji family, Taras is based in the wealthy city of Gasila and controls the important trade lifeline of the Nahasa Desert. In the Aserai confederacy established by Sultan Winged, his family occupies a prominent position due to its deep financial resources and control of the oasis. Talas's life has seen the decline of the Empire's influence and the rise of the Aserai tribes, and he knows how to dance between the various forces to preserve his family. He was not only a lord, but also an outstanding architect and businessman. The prosperity of Galzila was inseparable from his profound attainments in engineering and trade. Now, at the age of 48, he is carefully raising his four children, Farzana, Hafisa, Zu Eddard and Jalfa, and trying to consolidate the family's hereditary status through marriage and wealth on the turbulent continent of Calradia. Although he is currently loyal to Winged, he is always alert to the next beginning of the dance of power, ready to seize more benefits for the family.
